description: Wyoming-specific land access classification rules. These override national defaults where Wyoming has more specific data. Sources: Wyoming Game and Fish Department (WGFD), Wyoming Office of State Lands and Investments (OSLI). Rules receive a +1000 priority boost over national rules.

rules.source_dataset: Wyoming Game & Fish Department — Hunter Management Areas
rules.note: Wyoming Hunter Management Areas (HMAs) are private lands where WGFD holds access agreements for hunting. Access is permitted for licensed hunters during the agreement period. HMA enrollment changes annually — verify current boundaries and rules with WGFD before hunting.

rules.source_dataset: Wyoming Game & Fish Department — Walk-In Areas
rules.note: Wyoming Walk-In Area program lands are private properties with WGFD access agreements, open to hunting during the program season. Access is seasonal and enrollment changes annually — verify current Walk-In Area maps from WGFD.

rules.source_dataset: Wyoming Office of State Lands and Investments — State Trust Land
rules.note: Wyoming State Trust Land is generally open to public access and hunting under Wyoming state law (W.S. 36-5-105), unlike Colorado where state trust land defaults to closed. Verify that the specific parcel has not been closed by a grazing lease or other state order restricting access.

rules.source_dataset: Wyoming Game & Fish Department — Public Access Easements
rules.note: This parcel has a public access easement held by WGFD, making it open to the public for hunting and recreation even though underlying ownership may be private. Verify easement terms and boundaries with WGFD.

Checkerboard land ownership is common in Wyoming — alternating sections of BLM and private land in a grid pattern. Corner-crossing between diagonally adjacent BLM sections is legally contested. This polygon is in a checkerboard area; verify access carefully and consult current legal guidance before hunting near private corners.
